BRIDGE = rnpv.value_per_share()
SCENARIOS = S.scenarios()

BASE_RAW = BRIDGE["value_per_share_raw_chf"]

BASE_SARL = float(SCENARIOS.loc[SCENARIOS["scenario"] == "Base + SARL residual", "value_per_share"].iloc[0])
BULL = float(SCENARIOS.loc[SCENARIOS["scenario"] == "Bull", "value_per_share"].iloc[0])

RANGE_LO = float(SCENARIOS["value_per_share"].min())
RANGE_HI = float(SCENARIOS["value_per_share"].max())

# Fraction of base->market gap closed by Base+SARL scenario (user-requested replacement for the "two thirds" claim)

## TL;DR

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
**Base case fair value: CHF `{python} f"{BASE:.2f}"` / share (floored at zero).**
Equity value `{python} f"CHF {BRIDGE['equity_value_chf_m']:+,.0f} M"` pre-floor; current market **CHF `{python} f"{MARKET:.2f}"`** (IDIA.SW close `{python} MARKET_AS_OF`). Valuation date: `{python} A.VALUATION_DATE`.

**The base case is a conservative lower bound, not a price target.** The gap to the market decomposes into **two catalysts** the base case excludes: (1) a residual claim on the ring-fenced SARL assets (aprocitentan / selatogrel / cenerimod), and (2) a QUVIVIQ blockbuster trajectory above the base-case peak. On top of that sits **one refinancing event** the base case already treats as pure debt: the J&J convertible loan (CHF `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_PRINCIPAL_CHF_M:.0f}"` M, matures 15 Jun 2027, convertible into `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_SHARES_ON_CONVERSION_M:.1f}"` M shares at CHF `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_STRIKE_CHF:.2f}"`). The convertible is **never an upside**: either dilution if IDIA rerates above the strike, or a cash repayment at maturity.

**Reconciled fair-value range across scenarios: CHF `{python} f"{RANGE_LO:.2f}"` - `{python} f"{RANGE_HI:.2f}"` / share** (post-floor, post-if-converted). This is the single range used across all pages of this note.
:::

The three early-stage negative rNPVs reflect the arithmetic of applying a `{python} f"{A.cumulative_pos('phase2')*100:.1f} %"` Phase 2 cumulative to-approval probability against the phase-weighted development costs out to filing. They should be read as *"peak sales placeholder too low vs the phase-weighted dev spend"*, not as *"the programme should be discontinued"*. Phase 2 proof-of-concept readouts (CCR6 Q4 2026, CXCR3 2027, CXCR7 Q2 2028) will reanchor those figures materially in either direction.

```

**Parent net cash is negative** because we attribute `{python} f"CHF {A.PARENT_ATTRIBUTABLE_DEBT_CHF_M:.0f}"` M of debt to the parent equity holder (J&J convertible `{python} f"{A.DEBT_CONVERTIBLE_LOAN_JJ_CHF_M:.0f}"` + Pharmakon term loan `{python} f"{A.DEBT_PHARMAKON_LOAN_CHF_M:.0f}"` + convertible bonds `{python} f"{A.DEBT_CONVERTIBLE_BONDS_CHF_M:.0f}"` + other financial `{python} f"{A.DEBT_OTHER_FINANCIAL_CHF_M:.0f}"` incl. R-Bridge royalty monetization) against only `{python} f"CHF {A.PARENT_ATTRIBUTABLE_CASH_CHF_M:.0f}"` M of group cash (an upper bound at 30 Jun 2026 - see TODO_DATA.md). The CHF `{python} f"{A.DEBT_NOTES_SARL_CHF_M:.0f}"` M of SARL notes are excluded, they are non-recourse to IDIA shareholders and are serviced by the SARL assets.

The SARL New Money Facility (CHF 150 M nominal, CHF 105 M drawn at YE 2025) was repaid in full on 26 Jun 2026 from the first Pharmakon tranche, so it does not appear in the current debt line.

## What the valuation rides on

![](outputs/figures/tornado.png){fig-alt="Tornado chart of variables ranked by impact on value per share"}

Two variables dominate in the base case: **QUVIVIQ peak sales** and the **SARL residual assumption** (0 vs CHF 400 M). The central-costs upstream placeholder (+/-50 %, listed in TODO_DATA.md) is in the mid-tier of levers; discount rate and lucerastat PoS matter but do not move the needle on their own.

**Critical read**: no single variable at its stress case reaches the current market price. Closing the gap requires **multiple positive assumptions simultaneously**, that is the market's implicit bet.

![](outputs/figures/sensitivity_heatmap.png){fig-alt="Value-per-share heatmap over QUVIVIQ peak sales and discount rate"}

### DEA Schedule V update (not full descheduling)

On 11 Aug 2026, the DEA proposed to **reclassify DORAs (QUVIVIQ, Belsomra, Dayvigo) from Schedule IV to Schedule V**, not a full descheduling. Schedule V is the least-restrictive controlled substances tier (looser prescribing / refill constraints) but still a scheduled drug, so prescriber dispensing frictions are reduced without being eliminated. The upside scenarios in this note treat the reclassification as a *modest* commercial accelerator, not as a transformational catalyst. Source: [Marktpuls, Aug 2026](https://www.marktpuls.ch/artikel/permalink/675639).

### QUVIVIQ growth trajectory

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
hist = A.PRODUCTS["quviviq"]["historical_sales_chf_m"]
years = sorted(hist.keys())
growth_rows = []
for i, y in enumerate(years):
    if i == 0:
        growth_rows.append({"Year": y, "Net sales (CHF M)": hist[y], "YoY growth": "-"})
    else:
        g = (hist[y] / hist[years[i-1]] - 1.0) * 100.0
        growth_rows.append({"Year": y, "Net sales (CHF M)": hist[y], "YoY growth": f"{g:+.0f} %"})
print(pd.DataFrame(growth_rows).to_markdown(index=False))
```

Realised and guided QUVIVIQ growth is **not** a steady "~+50 % YoY" - it decelerated materially from +120 % (2024->2025) to +49 % guided (2025->2026). To reach the CHF `{python} f"{A.PRODUCTS['quviviq']['peak_sales_chf_m']:.0f}"` M peak by 2030 (an 8-year ramp from launch), 2026->2030 only needs ~`{python} f"{((A.PRODUCTS['quviviq']['peak_sales_chf_m']/200)**(1/4)-1)*100:.0f}"` % annual CAGR, which is consistent with growth decelerating further as the US DORA class matures and the EU reimbursement footprint fills in.

## Verdict

**The gap between the model and the market has widened, and so has the required set of assumptions behind the market price.**

The v1.1 base case floors at CHF `{python} f"{BASE:.2f}"` / share (raw equity value `{python} f"CHF {BRIDGE['equity_value_chf_m']:+,.0f} M"`). This is a hard lower bound under three jointly binding constraints: BIO 2011-2020 PoS transitions applied cleanly, QUVIVIQ margin ramping from the 2026 commercial-profitability target to a mid-range specialty 30 % at peak, and PV of unallocated central costs deducted from the equity bridge. The market at CHF `{python} f"{MARKET:.2f}"` therefore embeds assumptions that, on a probability-weighted basis, span the full range of upside paths:

- A **SARL residual** at least matching the CHF 400 M stressed in scenarios (not sufficient on its own to clear the zero floor under the current cost structure).
- A QUVIVIQ trajectory **well above** the CHF `{python} f"{A.PRODUCTS['quviviq']['peak_sales_chf_m']:.0f}"` M base-case peak (closer to the CHF 1,000 M Bull case) and a discount rate at the low end of the biotech WACC range.
- A clean **refinancing** of the CHF `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_PRINCIPAL_CHF_M:.0f}"` M J&J convertible on 15 June 2027: either cash repayment (reducing the equity bridge directly) or conversion if V/share exceeds CHF `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_STRIKE_CHF:.2f}"` (dilutive but debt-eliminating; the if-converted scenario is already applied in the Bull case and still prints CHF `{python} f"{BULL:.2f}"` / share).

**The reconciled range CHF `{python} f"{RANGE_LO:.2f}"` - `{python} f"{RANGE_HI:.2f}"` / share** is the honest answer under the method as corrected; the market price sits noticeably *above* even the Bull. That is not a claim IDIA is overvalued `{python} f"{MARKET/max(RANGE_HI, 0.01):.1f}"`×: it is a claim the market is pricing a combined scenario that is *outside* the parameter space our scenarios span (e.g. a QUVIVIQ peak above CHF 1,000 M, SARL residual above CHF 600 M, central cost normalisation faster than modelled, discount rate below 10 %).

**My reconciled personal read**: at CHF `{python} f"{MARKET:.2f}"`, IDIA is priced for a genuinely bullish composite outcome where (a) the DEA Schedule V reclassification, pediatric programme and EU reimbursement all contribute to a QUVIVIQ ceiling well above the CHF 600 M used here; (b) SARL asset performance clears the ring-fenced debt materially ahead of maturity; (c) the Pharmakon loan does not need to be extended on worse terms; and (d) the J&J convertible either converts (dilution absorbed by rerating) or is refinanced on terms that do not tighten covenants. Each of these is probabilistic; none is binary. The investable thesis is a *conditional long on specific catalyst delivery* (CCR6 PoC Q4 2026, QUVIVIQ US run-rate exit 2026, SARL progress disclosures) with limited margin of safety at the current level under the base case.

*Don't read any point estimate here as a price target.* Read the status column of each input, the four scenarios, and the gap-covered percentage. Every assumption is traceable; every scenario has an explicit narrative; every CHF of the gap between the model and the market can be tied to a specific bet or a specific placeholder.

## Limitations

- rNPV is an order-of-magnitude tool, not a precise valuation.
- Phase 2 peak sales (CCR6, CXCR7, CXCR3) are placeholders and drive their negative rNPVs. A positive CCR6 PoC readout at Q4 2026 would materially reshape those figures.
- The **J&J convertible is a cost, not an upside**: either dilution (if V/share > strike at maturity) or a CHF 335 M cash repayment on 15 Jun 2027. The if-converted test applies in scenarios where V/share > strike.
- **Central costs are modelled as a decline-then-floor-then-proportional curve** (71 M G&A sourced + 25 M upstream placeholder at year 1, decay 10 %/year to floor 50 M to 2040, then scaled by weighted revenue to 2050 with hard floor 10 M). Not a line-by-line projection.
- **Upstream research is deducted but no value is attributed to the unborn pipeline candidates** that upstream research will generate. This biases the model downward.
- **QUVIVIQ post-launch R&D** (pediatric programme, label extensions) is not modelled in either the per-product dev-cost curve (prelaunch only) or central costs.
- Working capital and capex are netted to zero; tax proxied by the operating margin; product outcomes are assumed independent.
- The SARL contingent liability to J&J (30 % aprocitentan + 10 % each selatogrel / cenerimod proceeds) is disclosed but not fully modelled, a known refinement.
- All historical data and the current share price are pinned to specific dates (`data/market.json` for the quote; `A.VALUATION_DATE = {python} A.VALUATION_DATE` for the balance sheet). Re-run `scripts/update_price.py` before each deploy.

Don't read any point estimate as a price target. Read the sourcing and the scenarios: every input has a status (sourced / assumption / placeholder), every scenario has an explicit narrative, and every CHF of the gap between the model and the market can be tied to a specific bet.
